events.system:
P = 4-(2-oxopropyl)benzonitrile
P --[Ph₃P=CH₂]--> Q
Q --[(i) CH₃MgBr; (ii) H₃O⁺]--> R
R --[dil. H₂SO₄]--> S
Q --[OsO₄, NMO]--> T
Q --[Br₂, H₂O]--> U
events.hidden_link: P is a ketone and a nitrile. Wittig on P reacts selectively at the ketone to give Q (alkene). Grignard on Q reacts at the nitrile, giving methyl ketone R after hydrolysis. Hydration of R gives S (Markovnikov addition, tertiary alcohol). Bromohydrin formation on Q gives U (OH on more substituted carbon).
events.route: 1. P undergoes Wittig olefination at the ketone to form Q (alkene). 2. CH3MgBr adds to the nitrile of Q, yielding a methyl ketone R upon hydrolysis. 3. Acid-catalysed hydration of the alkene in R follows Markovnikov's rule, placing the OH on the tertiary carbon to give S. 4. OsO4 gives syn-diol T. 5. Br2/H2O on Q forms a bromonium ion, which is opened by water at the more substituted carbon to yield halohydrin U.
events.student_must_notice: The regioselectivity in both the hydration of R to S and the bromohydrin formation from Q to U, which dictates whether the resulting alcohols are primary or tertiary.
events.trap: Students may form the anti-Markovnikov alcohol for S or open the bromonium ion at the less substituted carbon for U, both of which lead to primary alcohols that do not give immediate turbidity with Lucas reagent.
events.given: Reaction scheme with P provided by name.
events.asked: Reactivity with Lucas reagent and 2,4-DNP, and number of stereocentres.
events.why_hard: Requires correct application of regioselectivity rules in two separate electrophilic additions to an alkene to correctly predict the outcomes of the Lucas test.

question.text:
Consider the following reaction scheme starting with P (4-(2-oxopropyl)benzonitrile):

P → Q (via Ph₃P=CH₂)
Q → R (via (i) CH₃MgBr; (ii) H₃O⁺)
R → S (via dil. H₂SO₄)
Q → T (via OsO₄, NMO)
Q → U (via Br₂, H₂O)

Which of the following statements is/are correct?

options.A: Compound S gives immediate turbidity with Lucas reagent
options.B: Compound U gives immediate turbidity with Lucas reagent
options.C: Compound T contains exactly two stereocentres
options.D: Compound Q gives a positive 2,4-DNP test

members.name: granite-4.2-8b
members.working:
1. P = 4-(2-oxopropyl)benzonitrile: side chain CH2-CO-CH3 attached to benzene at para position.
2. Reaction with Ph3P=CH2 (a Wittig reagent) converts the carbonyl (C=O) of the 2-oxopropyl group into an alkene: CH2=CH-CH3 (allyl) attached to benzene via CH2? Actually Wittig on carbonyl gives CH2=CH- (attached to CH3). Starting chain: CH3-CO-CH2- attached to benzene? Wait 2-oxopropyl = CH2-CO-CH3? Actually 2-oxopropyl = CH2-CO-CH3 (prop-2-one) attached via CH2 to benzene: benzene-CH2-CO-CH3. Wittig on carbonyl gives benzene-CH2-CH=CH2 (allyl). So Q = 4-(allyl)benzonitrile (benzene-CH2-CH=CH2).
3. Q undergoes Grignard CH3MgBr then H3O+ to add methyl to the double bond? Grignard adds to alkene? Typically Grignard adds to carbonyl, but Q has no carbonyl now. However maybe the Grignard adds to the alkene via conjugate addition? More likely the Grignard adds to the nitrile? No, step (i) CH3MgBr then (ii) H3O+ likely adds methyl to the double bond giving a new stereocenter at the former alkene carbon. So R = 4-(2-methyl-2-propenyl?) Actually addition of methyl to allyl gives a secondary alcohol after protonation: CH2-CH(CH3)-CH2? Let's assume R is a secondary alcohol with one stereocenter.
4. R -- dilute H2SO4 --> S: acid-catalyzed hydration of double bond? But R already saturated? Might be dehydration? Actually S likely a tertiary alcohol after rearrangement? Lucas reagent (HCl/acetone) gives turbidity with tertiary alcohols immediate. S likely tertiary alcohol -> A true.
5. Q -- OsO4, NMO --> T: dihydroxylation of alkene to vicinal diol with two new stereocenters (cis). So T has two new stereocenters.
6. Q -- Br2, H2O --> U: bromination of alkene with water gives bromohydrin (addition of Br and OH across double bond) giving a single stereocenter (anti addition). So U has one stereocenter.
7. Lucas reagent reacts immediately with tertiary alcohols. S likely tertiary alcohol (if addition gave tertiary). U is bromohydrin with secondary/primary? Not tertiary, so B false.
8. Total stereocenters in S: likely one (the alcohol carbon). So C true.
9. R gives precipitate with 2,4-dinitrophenylhydrazine if it contains a ketone or aldehyde. R is alcohol, no carbonyl, so no precipitate. D false.
Thus correct statements: A and C.

members.name: glm-5.3-flash
members.working: P undergoes Wittig methylenation (Ph3P=CH2) converting the ketone to an exocyclic alkene: Q = p-NC-C6H4-CH2-C(CH3)=CH2. Q + CH3MgBr/H3O+ converts the nitrile to a methyl ketone: R = p-COCH3-C6H4-CH2-C(CH3)=CH2. R + dil. H2SO4 hydrates the alkene (Markovnikov) to tertiary alcohol S = p-COCH3-C6H4-CH2-C(OH)(CH3)2. Q + OsO4/NMO gives syn diol T; Q + Br2/H2O gives bromohydrin U = p-NC-C6H4-CH2-C(OH)(CH3)-CH2Br (tertiary alcohol). (A) S is tertiary alcohol: immediate Lucas turbidity - correct. (B) U is tertiary alcohol: immediate Lucas turbidity - correct. (C) In S the carbinol carbon has two identical CH3 groups, so 0 stereocentres, not 1 - incorrect. (D) R is a ketone, gives 2,4-DNPH precipitate - correct. Answer: ABD.
